tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, NO SENDS — planning only; every action this produces stays a draft behind the existing gateway.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 7 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these; the test file is new):
  server/pipeline/pipeline_queue.py
  server/pipeline/loop_tick.py
  tests/test_outreach_trigger.py

THE DEFECT, measured on live data minutes ago. Everything upstream now works and the last wire is missing:
  * The candidate feed has 9 real scored candidates (Bryan Wolynski 92, Dave Kading 90, Vishal Sud 88...).
  * queue_status()["alarm"]["level"] is "red" — zero guest cover, and the next Thursday slot is empty.
  * And the tick plans ZERO outreach actions. Executed proof:
        should_outreach: False | count: 8 | alarm: red | planned actions: 3 (all promotion_touch)
Why: should_outreach is still computed from the raw WIP count alone (count 8 >= TARGET_IN_FLIGHT 6 ->
"no new outreach"), while the cover alarm that knows the truth is ignored. The alarm is decorative.
That count of 8 is itself inflated — it includes already-published episodes and empty scaffolds — but
DO NOT fix the count in this lane; another change owns that. Fix the DECISION: a red cover alarm with
candidates on the shelf must produce outreach, whatever the WIP count says.

THE FIX:
1. pipeline_queue.queue_status: make should_outreach consider cover, not just WIP. Semantics, and put
   the reasoning in a comment citing this incident:
     * alarm level "red"  -> should_outreach True, ALWAYS (a red cover alarm means the pipeline cannot
       fill upcoming slots; WIP count is irrelevant when what is in flight cannot publish).
     * alarm level "warn" -> should_outreach True when the raw count is at or below target, i.e. the
       existing rule still applies, but warn never SUPPRESSES outreach that the count would have asked
       for.
     * alarm "ok"         -> existing count-based behaviour, unchanged.
   The returned "reason" string must state WHY in plain words a human reads in a daily log — name the
   alarm level and the driving condition (e.g. guest cover 0), not just the count. Keep every existing
   key in the returned dict; other modules and two scripts read them.
2. loop_tick.plan_tick: when outreach is warranted, it already ranks candidates via candidate_vetting
   and emits candidate_outreach actions — READ that code and keep its existing envelope, idempotency
   key, gating and dry-run behaviour EXACTLY as-is. The change here is only that the decision to enter
   that branch now follows queue_status's corrected should_outreach. Add a hard cap constant
   (MAX_OUTREACH_PER_TICK, small — the tick runs hourly and a red alarm must not fan out dozens of
   emails) with a comment saying why, and record any candidates NOT actioned because of the cap in the
   plan's "skipped" list with a reason. A cap that silently drops candidates is the banned pattern.
3. Nothing in this lane may send, and no action class may be promoted. Outreach stays whatever autonomy
   level its lane already has; you are producing plans, not permissions.

TESTS (tests/test_outreach_trigger.py; at least 7, fixed `now`, no network):
 (1) THE REAL CASE: a world with candidates available, WIP count above target, and a RED cover alarm ->
     should_outreach True and plan_tick emits at least one candidate_outreach action (this is the exact
     situation that produced zero actions on live data);
 (2) NEGATIVE: the same red alarm with ZERO candidates available emits no outreach action and records a
     skip naming the empty feed — a red alarm must never invent a target;
 (3) alarm "ok" with count above target -> no outreach (existing behaviour preserved);
 (4) alarm "warn" never suppresses outreach the count alone would have produced;
 (5) NEGATIVE: MAX_OUTREACH_PER_TICK is enforced and the overflow candidates appear in "skipped" with a
     cap reason (assert both the action count and the skip entries);
 (6) NEGATIVE: dry-run planning performs nothing (assert no dispatch/send fake is called) and the
     actions carry the same envelope keys the existing outreach path uses;
 (7) queue_status still returns every pre-existing key, and "reason" names the alarm level when the
     alarm drove the decision;
 (8) determinism: identical world + now -> identical plan including ordering.
Keep tests/test_pipeline_queue.py, tests/test_cover_alarm.py, tests/test_loop_tick.py,
tests/test_candidate_feed_wiring.py and tests/test_weekly_drumbeat.py green.
